newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai police hunt for Sanyo factory arsonists.
newsitem.headline: Thai police hunt for Sanyo factory arsonists.

text.p: Thai police said on Wednesday they were hunting for workers who ransacked and torched a warehouse and office of Sanyo Universal Electric Plc in the eastern outskirts of Bangkok after a dispute over bonuses.
They said several hundred Sanyo employees had rallied at the premises before the fire started on Tuesday in retaliation for reduced annual bonuses offered by the firm.

"According to witnesses and video tapes of the protest, about 20 workers resorted to burning the complex down. They apparently had planned the torching in advance," a police investigator told Reuters.
Witnesses said about 2,000 employees rallied on Tuesday to protest against the decision to cut the bonuses.
After the fire broke out, most workers fled the complex, they said.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who visited the fire scene late on Tuesday, said the incident had tarnished Thailand's image and could scare away foreign investors.
"So, this kind of protest that ends in violence should be the last one," he told reporters on Wednesday.
Sanyo Universal is owned 30 percent by Sanyo Electric Co Ltd of Japan while Thai partners own the remainder. It is a producer of refrigerators and other consumer appliances.
Trading in Sanyo's shares on the Thai bourse was suspended on Wednesday morning.
Sanyo said in a statement that its production line was unaffected by the fire.
"The fire will have no impact on the company's production as it caused no damage to the production line." it added.

Sanyo said the problem stemmed from employees' demand for a bonus of 5.75 months' salary this year despite the company's announcement of a three-month payment because the firm had been hit by a recession.
"This offended some groups of employees who later led a rally within the company, leading to the fire at the warehouse building for finished products and parts of the office building," it added.
"All items have been insured. The damage is presently being estimated by the insurance company," it said.
Police said no arrests had been made.
"This is not a complicated case. But I think we can catch them in a couple of days," the police investigator said.
